items.title: The parabolic Hecke module and the antispherical standard basis
items.statement: Work with the normalized type-$A$ Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]: generators $H_s$ with $H_s^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_s$, standard basis $\{H_w:w\in S_n\}$, bar involution $\overline{H_s}=H_s^{-1}=H_s-(v^{-1}-v)$ and Kazhdan-Lusztig basis $\{\underline H_w\}$ of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] (so that $\underline H_s=H_s+v$). Fix $J\subseteq S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$, let $W_J=\langle s:s\in J\rangle\subseteq S_n$ be the standard parabolic subgroup and let $\Phi_J=\Phi\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\alpha_s:s\in J\}$ be its standard type-A root subsystem, all in the conventions of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]. Two characters of the parabolic Hecke algebra $H_J\subseteq H_v(n)$ are used. For $s\in J$ the quadratic relation makes $v^{-1}$ and $-v$ the two roots of $x^2-(v^{-1}-v)x-1=0$, so there are well-defined algebra homomorphisms $\varphi_{+},\varphi_{-}:H_J\to A$ with $\varphi_+(H_s)=v^{-1}$ and $\varphi_-(H_s)=-v$ for all $s\in J$ (they respect the braid relations because they are scalar on the generators). Viewing $A$ through $\varphi_+$ (resp. $\varphi_-$) as a right $H_J$-module gives the **spherical parabolic module** $M^J:=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$ and the **antispherical parabolic module** $N^J:=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$, right $H_v(n)$-modules under right multiplication on the second factor. Throughout, $\Phi^+$ is the positive system of $\Phi$ and $\Phi_J^+=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^+$, and $$^JW:=\{w\in S_n:\ell(sw)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\},\qquad W^J:=\{w\in S_n:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\}$$ are the minimal left and right coset representatives; by [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] and [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] every $w\in S_n$ factors uniquely as $w=l y$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(l)+\ell(y)$, and inversion interchanges ${^JW}$ and $W^J$. The definitions of $\varphi_\pm$ use only the quadratic relation on generators; no further module-theoretic input enters.
items.strategy: Conventions and well-definedness only. The signs $v^{-1},-v$ solve $t^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)t$ by direct expansion ([[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]), so $\varphi_\pm$ are algebra maps because the Hecke relations in a single factor are generated by the quadratic relations together with the braid relations, on which scalars act trivially. The coset statements are the standard parabolic factorization of [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] and [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]]; inversion preserves length and interchanges left and right descents, so ${^JW}^{-1}=W^J$. The bases $\{1\otimes H_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ and the right action formulas are asserted nowhere here: they are the content of [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]]. The spherical module is recorded because the singular-block multiplicities are read in the spherical normalization; the antispherical module is recorded because its canonical basis is the induced-sign analogue and its coefficients differ in general.

items.title: The singular integral block and its dot stabilizer
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r$, Weyl group $W$, Weyl vector $\rho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, as in [[def-bgg-category-o]] and [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]. A weight $\mu$ is **dot-antidominant** if $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ and **integral** if $\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ for all $i$ ([[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]], [[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]). Fix such a weight $\mu$ and put $J=J(\mu):=\{i:\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\}$ and $W_\mu:=W_J=\langle s_i:i\in J\rangle$; then the dot stabilizer $\{v\in W:v\cdot\mu=\mu\}$ equals $W_J$ (the inclusion $W_J\subseteq$ stabilizer holds because each $s_i$, $i\in J$, fixes $\mu+\rho$; equality follows since the stabilizer of an integral antidominant weight is generated by the reflections it contains and is a standard parabolic, [[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]]). The **singular integral block** $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the block of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] of the central character of $\mu$; its simple objects $L(w\cdot\mu)$, standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)=M(w\cdot\mu)$, costandard objects $\nabla(w\cdot\mu)$ and projective covers $P(w\cdot\mu)$ are indexed by $w\in W$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-verma-module]]), and $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ if and only if $w'\in wW_J$. Hence the labels can be normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $w\in W^J=\{w:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \forall s\in J\}$, and inversion carries $W^J$ onto ${^JW}$ of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]]. The block is a highest-weight category with the standard and simple classes as bases of its Grothendieck group ([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]), it satisfies BGG reciprocity $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]$, and the multiplicity matrix is unitriangular for the refinement of the dominance order on the dot orbit ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]). The block is **regular** when $J=\varnothing$ (no wall) and **singular** when $J\neq\varnothing$; the singular translation statements use this notation, and $J=\varnothing$ recovers the regular case. The genuine regular-parabolic multiplicity statements below have their separate explicit dominant regular base.
items.strategy: Conventions and inherited structure only. The stabilizer claim uses the standard fact that for an integral dot-antidominant weight the dot stabilizer is the standard parabolic generated by the simple reflections it contains ([[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]], applied to the dominant vector -mu-rho); the coset description of the label set is $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu\iff w^{-1}w'\in W_\mu\iff w'\in wW_J$. The block theory, the index set $W$, the highest-weight structure, the Grothendieck bases and BGG reciprocity are quoted from the published items; no new multiplicity assertion is made here. The normalization by $W^J$ (rather than $W$) is recorded exactly because it matches the minimal coset representatives of the parabolic Hecke modules and the inversion dictionary $W^J={^JW}^{-1}$. The finite singular block inherits enough projective covers and ordinary Verma flags from the actual published items. BGG gives diagonal standard multiplicity1 and only standards above each head. Canonical maximal-weight Verma traces remove higher factors; the remaining labelled Verma quotient has higher-Verma-filtered kernel, giving the highest-weight data. The actual ordinary standard/costandard Hom and Ext1 supplier applies to these ordinary Vermas; this is not the later generalized-Verma restriction. The published Grothendieck-bases theorem supplies the stated simple/standard bases.

items.title: Standard parabolic and Levi subalgebras from a subset of simple roots
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the published root-space/sl2 suppliers. Let g be finite-dimensional complex semisimple with Cartan h, roots Phi, positives Phi^+, simple roots alpha_i, and J a subset of the simple indices. Put Phi_J=Phi intersect span_R{alpha_j:j in J}, H_j=the coroot of alpha_j, h_J=span_C{H_j:j in J} and z_J={h:alpha_j(h)=0 for all j in J}. Define s_J=h_J plus the root spaces of Phi_J, l_J=h plus those root spaces, u_J=the sum of positive root spaces outside Phi_J, and p_J=l_J plus u_J. Then h=h_J direct-sum z_J, s_J is semisimple with roots Phi_J, and l_J=s_J direct-sum z_J is reductive with center z_J, Cartan h and Weyl group W_J. The sums l_J,u_J,p_J are Lie subalgebras, u_J is the nilradical of p_J, and p_J=l_J semidirect u_J is its reductive parabolic Levi decomposition. In the published radical-based sense of def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition, rad(p_J)=z_J plus u_J and s_J is the SEMISIMPLE Levi factor complementing that radical; l_J need not be semisimple. The parabolic contains b and equals b plus the negative Phi_J root spaces. For J empty it is b; for J all it is g. There exists zeta in z_J with alpha_i(zeta)=1 outside J, giving u_J strictly positive integral degrees and v_J (the outside negative radical) strictly negative degrees, with l_J degree0. Both radicals have finite-dimensional fixed-degree PBW slices. The construction depends only on the positive system and J.
items.strategy:
Put h_J=span{H_j:j∈J}, z_J={h:α_j(h)=0 for all j∈J}. The finite-type Cartan
principal submatrix is nonsingular because its symmetrized Gram matrix is
positive definite. Thus h=h_J⊕z_J. Set
s_J=h_J⊕⊕_{α∈Φ_J}g_α, l_J=s_J⊕z_J, and
u_J=⊕_{β∈Φ^+\Φ_J^+}g_β, v_J=⊕_{β∈Φ^-\Φ_J^-}g_β.
For alpha in Phi_J its Killing-dual vector, hence its rescaled coroot, lies in h_J by linearity of the Killing dual of the J-root expansion. Thus opposite root brackets lie in h_J. Root brackets make s_J,l_J,u_J,p_J=l_J⊕u_J and v_J Lie subalgebras, with
u_J ideal in p_J and l_J stabilizing u_J and v_J.

The INTRINSIC Killing form of s_J on h_J is Σ_{α∈Φ_J}α(h)α(h'); on the real
coroot span this is positive definite since the roots span its dual. Weight
orthogonality pairs only opposite root spaces; invariance and a root sl2 triple
give K(e_α,f_α)=K(H_α,H_α)/2≠0. Hence this Killing form is nondegenerate,
and the actual Cartan criterion proves s_J semisimple. The centralizer z_J
commutes with s_J, so l_J is reductive and has root system Φ_J and Weyl group W_J.

Choose ζ with α_j(ζ)=0 for j∈J and α_i(ζ)=1 for i∉J. Positive radical roots
have positive integral ζ-degree; negative outside roots have negative degree;
Levi roots have degree0. Thus u_J is nilpotent by its positive grading.
Its nilradical equality requires more than saying l_J is reductive. A nilpotent
ideal I in p_J projects to an ideal of l_J, whose projection into semisimple s_J
is zero. If its remaining image contains nonzero h∈z_J, lift h to x=h+a, a∈u_J.
Some outside simple root has α_i(h)≠0. In the ζ-grading, ad x is upper triangular
with diagonal ad h and has that nonzero eigenvalue. Its corresponding generalized
eigenspace lies in im(ad x)⊂I; hence ad x on I has a nonzero eigenvalue, impossible
for a nilpotent I. So I⊂u_J. Also rad(p_J)=z_J⊕u_J: this is a solvable ideal with
semisimple quotient s_J. Therefore l_J is the REDUCTIVE complement to nilradical,
whereas s_J is the semisimple Levi factor in the published radical-based Definition.
The cases J=empty and J=all have s_J=0 or u_J=v_J=0 as appropriate.

items.title: Standard bases, right actions and bar involutions on the parabolic Hecke modules
items.statement:
Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and put $m_x:=1\otimes H_x$, $n_x:=1\otimes H_x$ for $x\in{^JW}$, and $C_s:=\underline H_s=H_s+v$ for $s\in S$. (1) (Bases.) The sets $\{m_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ and $\{n_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$ respectively: indeed every $w\in S_n$ factors uniquely as $w=ly$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$, length-additively, and $\varphi_\pm(H_l)=\varphi_\pm(H_s)^{\ell(l)}\in\{v^{-\ell(l)},\pm v^{\ell(l)}\}$ is a unit of $A$, so $1\otimes H_w=\varphi_\pm(H_l)\,(1\otimes H_y)$ in both modules. (2) (Right action.) For $s\in S$ and $x\in{^JW}$: $$m_x C_s= egin{cases}m_{xs}+v\,m_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs>x,\ m_{xs}+v^{-1}m_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs<x,\ (v+v^{-1})m_x,&xs
otin{^JW},\end{cases}\qquad n_xC_s= egin{cases}n_{xs}+v\,n_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs>x,\ n_{xs}+v^{-1}n_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs<x,\ 0,&xs
otin{^JW}.\end{cases}$$ (3) (Bar.) The assignment $a\otimes h\mapsto  ar a\otimes ar h$ (bar on $A$ and the bar involution of $H_v(n)$) descends to $A$-antilinear involutions of $M^J$ and $N^J$ that satisfy $\overline{X\cdot h}=\overline X\cdot ar h$ and $\overline{m_x}=m_x+\sum_{y<x}a_{y,x}m_y$, $\overline{n_x}=n_x+\sum_{y<x}b_{y,x}n_y$ with $a_{y,x},b_{y,x}\in A$ and $a_{x,x}=b_{x,x}=1$; the top coefficient is one. (4) (Parabolic property.) If $x\in{^JW}$ and $s\in S$ with $xs
otin{^JW}$ then $xs=rx$ for a unique simple $r\in J$ and $xs>x$.
items.strategy: H is free as a LEFT H_J-module with basis H_y for y in ^J W: its standard basis partitions into the length-additive products H_u H_y for u in W_J, and uniqueness of parabolic factorization gives independent blocks. Tensoring this free decomposition with either rank-one character gives the asserted bases; units alone do not prove independence. The standard multiplication rule gives the two minimal branches. For the remaining branch prove the needed type-A parabolic property directly: J partitions the values into contiguous blocks, and x is left-minimal exactly when values in each block occur in increasing order in its one-line notation. A neighboring-position swap can violate this only when the entries are consecutive values a,a+1 of one block; then xs_j=s_a x, with s_a in J and xs_j>x. Thus H_x H_s=H_xs=H_r H_x, with NO decreasing-length correction. Consequently n_x C_s=(-v+v)n_x=0 and m_x C_s=(v^-1+v)m_x. The character maps commute with bar, since phi_-(bar H_s)=-v^-1 and phi_+(bar H_s)=v, the conjugates of their respective values; hence the balanced bar descends and is multiplicatively compatible. Ordinary bar satisfies bar H_x=H_{x^-1}^-1=H_x+sum_{z<x}c_z H_z with c_z in A, not a pure-negative-degree assertion. This follows by expanding inverse simple generators along a reduced word: all proper subexpressions have smaller Bruhat labels. If z=u y is its parabolic factorization then y<=z<x by the subword property, so collecting cosets proves the induced triangular bar and its top coefficient1. The exact finite combinatorics and Hecke rules are recorded in section8 of the owner proof note.

items.title: The facet tensor-weight exclusion lemma
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be an integral dot-antidominant dot-regular weight and let $\mu$ be an integral dot-antidominant weight such that the facet $F_\mu$ lies in the closure of the chamber $F_\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ for the positive roots $\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ of the parabolic subsystem $\Phi_J$ of $J=J(\mu)$ defined in [[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]], and $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ has the same sign as $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for every remaining positive root. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant weight of the linear orbit $W(\mu-\lambda)$ ([[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]]) and let $E=L(\nu)$ ([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]). Then for all $w,w'\in W$ and every weight $\gamma$ of $E$: if $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\lambda+\gamma$, then $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ and $\gamma=w(\mu-\lambda)$. Consequently, for every $w$ the tensor $E\otimes\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has exactly one Verma factor whose central character is that of $\mu$, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, and its multiplicity in the Verma flag computed by [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]] is one.
items.strategy: The proof is the published single-wall proof of [[lem-single-wall-tensor-weight-exclusion]] with the stabilizer $\{1,s\}$ replaced by the full dot stabilizer $W_J$; only the last step changes. Write $\lambda_\bullet=\lambda+\rho$, $\mu_\bullet=\mu+\rho$. From $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\lambda+\gamma$ one gets $(w')^{-1}\gamma=\mu_\bullet-x\lambda_\bullet$ with $x=(w')^{-1}w$; the norm bound $|\gamma|\le|\nu|=|\mu_\bullet-\lambda_\bullet|$ ([[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) and the dominant distance comparison for the dominant vectors $-\mu_\bullet,-\lambda_\bullet$ ([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]]) give equality throughout; the equality case gives $x(-\lambda_\bullet)\in \operatorname{Stab}_W(-\mu_\bullet)(-\lambda_\bullet)=W_J\,(-\lambda_\bullet)$, so $x\lambda_\bullet\in W_J\lambda_\bullet$, and since $\lambda_\bullet$ is regular, $x\in W_J$. Hence $x\cdot\mu=\mu$ (because $W_J$ is the dot stabilizer) and $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$, and $\gamma=w(\mu-\lambda)$; the multiplicity-one clause is [[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]. The central-character clause uses [[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]. The Choice assumption is inherited from the published translation and norm items; no new choice principle is used.

items.title: Parabolic category O for a standard parabolic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published category-O theory. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard parabolic of [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$, and $W_J$ its Weyl group. A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant** if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all $\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular $\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$). For such a $\lambda$ let $E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight $\lambda$ ([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]) by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero, and define the **generalized Verma module** $$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$ The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which $U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely; its objects are exactly the modules $M\in\mathcal O$ such that every vector lies in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule. For each $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the module $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, has highest weight $\lambda$, and $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of the Verma module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$ $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral, and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$. The costandard objects are $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, naturally submodules of the ordinary dual Vermas. They need not be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.
items.strategy:
Finite l_J modules with h-semisimple action split into center-weight spaces and
then finite simple s_J modules by actual Weyl complete reducibility. Its finite
simples E(η) are parametrized by η integral dominant on J; center acts by η|z_J.
Inflate E to p by u=0. PBW gives Δ^J(η)=U(v_J)⊗E(η). Each bounded negative
ζ-degree piece is finite dimensional and Levi-stable; positive u raises ζ-weight
and hence lowers this degree after PBW reordering, annihilating E at degree0.
Thus these finite pieces are p-stable. This proves p-local finiteness directly.
The natural ordinary Verma surjection shows Δ^J belongs to O and has unique
simple head L(η), one-dimensional top, finite length, and only lower factors.

Inside O, p-local finiteness is equivalent to local nilpotence of every f_j,j∈J.
Necessity uses finite h-weight support of a finite p-module. Conversely a cyclic
Levi submodule is an O-module for s_J: finite center weights, h-semisimplicity,
and local n_J^+-finiteness are inherited. Its finite composition series has
integrable simples, which are finite dimensional by the proved highest-weight
classification; hence it is finite dimensional. Then U(p)m=U(l)U(u)m is finite
because U(u)m is finite in O and each of its finitely many generators is Levi-finite.
Local nilpotence passes through subobjects, quotients and extensions, proving
Serre closure. This proof does not assume extensions of local-finite modules
are automatically local finite for an arbitrary algebra.

A simple highest weight lies in O^p iff its highest weight is J-dominant integral:
necessity is finite Levi highest-weight classification; sufficiency is its quotient
of Δ^J. In any p-finite quotient of Δ(η), the highest vector generates the finite
Levi simple E(η), and u kills it and its Levi span. The induced universal property
forces factorization through Δ^J(η). This is the largest p-finite quotient.
Restricted duality preserves O^p: a locally finite semisimple Levi representation
with finite h-weight spaces is an algebraic direct sum of finite Levi simples
(using an increasing sequence of finite Levi submodules and finite complete reducibility); PBW and finitely many g-generators give a countable spanning list. Its successive finite Levi spans exhaust M; finite complete reducibility splits each inclusion, giving the stated direct sum without importing an infinite semisimplicity theorem. Every weight meets only finitely many summands by finite weight dimension, so its restricted dual is the direct sum of the finite restricted duals. Thus ∇^J(η)=DΔ^J(η) is p-finite and its simple socle is L(η).
It is a submodule of ordinary DΔ(η), not generally a quotient.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]]. For every $x\in{^JW}$ there is a unique $C_x\in M^J$ and a unique $D_x\in N^J$ with (i) $\overline{C_x}=C_x$ and $\overline{D_x}=D_x$, and (ii) $C_x\in m_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,m_y$, $D_x\in n_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,n_y$, the sums over the lower Bruhat ideal of $x$ inside ${^JW}$. The sets $\{C_x\}_{x\in{^JW}}$ and $\{D_x\}_{x\in{^JW}}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$. No coefficientwise positivity is asserted.
items.strategy: The triangular induction of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] applies verbatim over the finite Bruhat ideal, because the only inputs are the bar involution and the fact that the bar of a standard basis element has top term itself with coefficient one and lies in the span of lower standard elements: for $\overline{m_x}=m_x+\sum_{y<x}a_{y,x}m_y$ as in [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]], one defines the coefficients of $C_x$ by descending induction on $\ell(x)$ through the finite interval $\{y\in{^JW}:y\le x\}$, using the bar-duality equation; anti-invariance splits each coefficient into its positive- and negative-degree parts (the two intersections $v\mathbb Z[v]\cap v^{-1}\mathbb Z[v^{-1}]=0$), and the same uniqueness argument on a Bruhat-maximal support element applies. The sphere of the argument is dimension-free and finite, and no choice principle is used. The proof of the existence statement in [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] is the template; only the coefficient recursion changes its indexing set from $S_n$ to ${^JW}$.

items.title: Translation to the wall on Verma, simple and projective objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]: $\lambda$ integral dot-antidominant and dot-regular, $\mu$ integral dot-antidominant with $F_\mu$ in the closure of the chamber $F_\lambda$, $J=J(\mu)$, $W_\mu=W_J$. Let $
u$ be the unique dominant weight of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and let $$T:=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(L(
u)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\mu,\qquad T':=T_\mu^\lambda,$$ be the translation functors of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], which are exact and biadjoint ([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]). Then: (1) $T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and $T
abla(w\cdot\lambda)\cong
abla(w\cdot\mu)$ for every $w\in W$. (2) $TL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu)$ if $w\in W^J$, and $TL(w\cdot\lambda)=0$ otherwise; equivalently $TL(w\cdot\lambda)
eq0$ if and only if the facet $F_{w\cdot\mu}$ is contained in the upper closure $F^+_{w\cdot\lambda}$ of [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]. (3) (Big projective on the wall.) Let $\Xi_\mu:=T_{-ho}^{\mu}L(-ho)$ be the translate of the simple object of the most singular block. Then $\Xi_\mu$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O_\mu$, it is the projective cover $P(1\cdot\mu)$ of $L(\mu)$, and $(\Xi_\mu:\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$ for every distinct orbit label (equivalently for its representatives $w\in W^J$); consequently $(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for every distinct label $y\in W^J$ and $[\Delta(w\cdot\mu):L(\mu)]=1$ for all $w\in W$.
items.strategy:
Facet weight exclusion gives TΔ_w=Δ'_w. Finite-dimensional restricted duality fixes E, and finite tensor/weight duality gives D(E tensor M)=E tensor DM; generalized central blocks are dual-stable. Thus restricted-duality compatibility gives
T∇_w=∇'_w. Exactness gives Δ'_w→TL_w→∇'_w. If TL_w is nonzero, its image is
nonzero in the one-dimensional Hom(Δ'_w,∇'_w) and is the simple L'_w. For a
nonminimal w in W/W_J, a proper Verma embedding Δ_{ws}→Δ_w with ws<w,
s∈J, translates to a nonzero map between identical Vermas, hence an isomorphism;
nonzero follows by exactness preserving this injection. Therefore TL_w=0. A
composition series of Δ_w for minimal w must account for L'_w; among its coset
only this minimal w can survive, so TL_w=L'_w. This proves the exact survival
matrix, without claiming every quotient of a simple-head Verma is simple.

The most-singular Δ(-ρ)=L(-ρ) is projective by its top-weight functor and is
injective by duality; its one-simple block is semisimple. Translate it to the
antidominant singular μ using E highest w0(μ+ρ). Norm/extremal weights give one
standard for each DISTINCT orbit label, once. The translate Q is projective-injective.
Reverse adjunction computes Hom(Q,L(μ))=1: E* has highest weight -(μ+ρ), which
is the sole weight giving the projected most-singular Verma in E*Δ(μ).
Thus P(μ) occurs in Q. Every singular Δ(y·μ) contains the simple Δ(μ) by the BGG
embedding criterion; reciprocity forces every standard in P(μ) at least once.
The Q flag has each once, so Q=P(μ) and all these multiplicities are1. Other
projectives need not contain all standards; the native universal ≥1 clause is false.

items.title: Parabolic category O is a highest weight category
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then: (1) (Simples.) Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form. (2) (Standards.) For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and $[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]
eq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of $M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. (3) (Enough projectives.) The inclusion $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint $L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient); $L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$ to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object $P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives. (4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.) Every projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda,\mu$, $$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$ the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $
abla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),
abla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$ for all $\lambda,\mu$.
items.strategy:
For finite-length M, take a kernel K of MINIMAL length among kernels with M/K
p-finite (zero quotient is allowed). If K' is any other such kernel, M/(K∩K')
embeds in the finite product M/K⊕M/K', hence is p-finite. Minimality gives K⊂K'.
Therefore K is the intersection of all these kernels and gives the largest quotient
L_p M. This is a functor left adjoint to exact inclusion; it is right exact and
sends ordinary projectives to parabolic projectives. The quotient L_p P(η) maps
onto L(η) and this map is essential: the preimage in ordinary P(η) of any subobject
surjecting to L(η) is all of P(η). Thus it is the parabolic projective cover.

Flags require an independent construction. Fix an integral central-character block
and its finite dot orbit bounded by its dot-dominant κ. The dominant weight κ+ρ has κ+ρ−w(κ+ρ) in Q^+, so every orbit label is<=κ. Every object of the block has finite length and all its simple highest weights are in that orbit; hence all its weights are<=κ and its ζ-weights are<=κ(ζ). This supplies the exact block bound, also for singular integral blocks. For a Levi simple E(η)
from a target label, N=κ(ζ)−η(ζ) is a nonnegative integer. Form the finite p-module
B_N(E)=U(p)⊗_{U(l)}E modulo all u-PBW degrees>N. The cutoff is p-stable. This
module represents Hom_l(E,-) on p-finite modules whose ζ-weights are≤κ(ζ): every
excluded positive monomial kills a map's image of E. Hom_l(E,-) is exact here:
lift its finitely many generators through an epimorphism inside a finite Levi
submodule and use finite complete reducibility to split. Induce and project to
the chosen central block: Q(E)=pr_χ(U(g)⊗_p B_N(E)). PBW induction and block
projection are exact, so Q is projective in that parabolic block.

The radical-degree filtration of B_N has finite semisimple Levi slices, on which
u acts by0. Its induced factors are finite direct sums of generalized Vermas.
Projection retains a finite generalized-standard flag. These Q cover every simple,
since its highest Levi E maps into that simple. For a constructed parabolic cover,
a lifted Q→P^p hitting its simple head is onto by essentiality and splits by
projectivity. Hence every projective cover is a summand of a finite sum of Q's.

For a maximal flag label η, the canonical trace U(g)X^η is
Δ^J(η)⊗X^η, with generalized-standard quotient. Prove this by induction on the
original flag. A last non-η quotient has zero η weight; a last η quotient splits
by lifting its top weight, which is highest, whose Levi span is E(η) and whose
u-action vanishes. Every endomorphism preserves this trace, and its projector
acts on the finite multiplicity space. The quotient has a shorter flag; induction
proves direct summands retain generalized-standard flags. This supplies the missing
projective flags without applying a merely right-exact reflector to ordinary flags.

Hom(Δ^J(η),DΔ^J(ξ)) injects into Hom(Δ(η),DΔ(ξ)) by the ordinary quotient and
costandard submodule maps. Thus it is0 unless η=ξ and at most1 then. For equal
labels the nonzero map Δ^J→L(η)→DΔ^J gives dimension1; its image is simple.
For an extension0→DΔ^J(ξ)→X→Δ^J(η)→0, if η is not strictly below ξ, X has no
weight strictly above η. Lift the top η vector: it is highest, its Levi span is
E(η), and u annihilates it, so it induces a section of the standard quotient.
If η<ξ, dualizing reduces to the first case. This includes incomparable labels.
Therefore Ext1 inside O^p vanishes; no restriction of ordinary Ext is presumed.

For a generalized-standard flag of P^p, induction using this Hom/Ext vanishing
identifies its Δ^J(ξ) multiplicity with dim Hom(P^p,∇^J(ξ)). Projectivity and a
composition series compute this dimension as [∇^J(ξ):L(η)]=[Δ^J(ξ):L(η)] because
simple restricted duals are fixed. This proves BGG reciprocity. The standard
support is ξ≥η and diagonal1. Removing the maximal higher traces gives the cover's
surjection to Δ^J(η) with higher-standard-filtered kernel, the highest-weight axiom.
Duality supplies enough injectives. Simple/standard Grothendieck bases and character
injectivity follow from their finite unitriangular highest-weight matrix.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases and polynomials
items.statement: Retain the notation of the preceding items and write the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] as $$C_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{^JW}}m_{y,x}\,m_y,\qquad D_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{^JW}}n_{y,x}\,n_y,\qquad x\in{^JW},$$ with coefficients $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z[v]$ supported on the lower Bruhat ideal, $m_{x,x}=n_{x,x}=1$ and $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<x$. The **spherical parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials** are $M^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}m_{y,x}$ with $q=v^{-2}$, and the **antispherical (sign) parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials** are $N^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}n_{y,x}$; the parity and degree bounds established in [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]] make these polynomials in $q$. Normalization dictionary (the exact Deodhar normalization): with $P^J_{y,x}(u)$ the parabolic polynomials of Deodhar (1987) attached to the subset $J$, one has $M^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=-1$ and $N^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=q$, in the index convention of Deodhar and of the anti-spherical category. Values at $v=1$ are written $m_{y,x}(1)$, $n_{y,x}(1)$. The spherical coefficients reduce to ordinary ones: if $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\,w_0^J x}$ for all $y,x\in{^JW}$, where $p$ is the coefficient of the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
items.strategy: Define m,n as the canonical-basis coefficients already constructed. Their support/diagonal and vZ[v] properties are supplied by the basis theorem. The shifted q-polynomials and the displayed spherical reduction are forward well-definedness claims discharged by the following reduction theorem, declared in justified_by: that proof uses only these m,n coefficients and induced modules, not a presupposed q-polynomial property. Spherical coefficients are ordinary p_{wJ y,wJ x}; antispherical coefficients are sums (-v)^ell(u) p_{uy,x}, with ell(uy)=ell(u)+ell(y). Ordinary coefficient parity and maximal v-degree ell(x)-ell(y) therefore give the corresponding parity and degree bound for both families. Multiplying by v^(ell(y)-ell(x)) leaves only nonpositive even exponents, so it is a polynomial in q=v^-2. The stated Deodhar u=-1 versus u=q dictionary matches Libedinsky–Williamson §2.6; spherical is trivial-character induction and antispherical is sign-character induction. No nonexistent parity clause of the previous existence theorem is cited.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials are alternating sums of ordinary ones
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]. (1) (Antispherical alternating sum.) For all $x,y\in{^JW}$, $$n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}\,v^{\ell(z)}\,p_{zy,\,x},$$ the sum over all $z\in W_J$ (the product $zy$ taken in $S_n$, and $p_{\cdot,x}$ the ordinary coefficient of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so the inner coefficients vanish unless $zy\le x$). (2) (Spherical reduction.) If $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then for all $x,y\in{^JW}$ $$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\ w_0^J x}.$$ In particular both families are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, with no separate recursion.
items.strategy:
For antispherical reduction, Φ(underlineH_x) has coefficients
Σ_u(-v)^ℓu p_{uy,x}; every lower supported term has uy<x, since x,y are minimal
and in distinct cosets. Hence all lower coefficients lie in vZ[v] directly,
and uniqueness identifies this with D_x. For spherical reduction let
C_J=Σ_u∈WJ v^{ℓwJ−ℓu}H_u. Pairing u with us or su gives left/right H_s eigenvalue
v^-1. Bar preserves these equations and top coefficient1, so C_J is bar-fixed,
and ordinary KL uniqueness identifies it with underlineH_wJ. The map
1⊗h→C_Jh identifies M with the eigen-subspace C_JH. Ordinary underlineH_wJx
has these left eigenvalues by the ordinary KL descent multiplication formula.
Comparing top coefficients on C_JH_y gives exactly p_{wJ y,wJ x}; bar and
triangularity identify it with C_x. The ordinary coefficient degree bound then
gives parity ℓx−ℓy and exponent at most that length difference in both families;
for the antispherical formula ℓuy=ℓu+ℓy. Thus the shifted coefficients are
polynomials in q=v^-2. This well-definedness is proved by the reduction, not an
unstated parity clause of the existence theorem.

 The required coset order comparison is proved by subwords: if y<=x are minimal, prefix a fixed reduced wJ to a subword expression to get wJ y<=wJ x. Conversely a subword of wJ x with product wJ y splits into a J-word followed by a subword z of x. Parabolic projection sends that product and z to the same minimum y; length-additive factorization gives y<=z, and deletion reduces z within the x-subword, so z<=x. Thus y<=x iff wJ y<=wJ x, proving the triangular support of the spherical candidate. Right multiplication by global w0 reverses Bruhat covers because it sends length ell(a) to ell(w0)-ell(a) and keeps the same left reflection; hence it reverses the full order. This proves the order-reversing iota and k dictionaries used below, with no unproved label-mirror assertion.

items.title: Singular category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work in the type-$A$
root datum $W=S_n$ of the page's Hecke module and ordinary multiplicity
theorem. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]
with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of
[[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels
normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be
the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$,
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,\,ww_0}(1),$$
the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial attached to the
pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
Equivalently, put $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0\in{}^JW$. Then
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1).$$
This is the spherical family. The antispherical family instead governs the
genuine regular parabolic locally finite category with dominant labels;
changing to an opposite positive system does not identify the two families.
In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial
coefficients beyond the value at one occur.
items.strategy:
Apply exact T to a composition series of the regular Delta(y dot lambda_anti). A regular simple contributes the singular L(w dot mu) only when its label lies in wW_J; among that coset the proved survival theorem keeps exactly the unique minimal right representative w. Thus this singular multiplicity equals the regular [Delta(y dot lambda_anti):L(w dot lambda_anti)]. Relative to the dominant base, the two regular labels are y w0 and w w0. Published ordinary BGG gives the projective-standard version. Therefore exact T and the regular KL theorem give [Δ(y·μ):L(w·μ)]=P_{yw0,ww0}(1) for
minimal right representatives y,w. To express this in the fixed LEFT spherical
module use k(w)=wJ w^-1 w0∈^J W. Its validity follows by reversing left descents
with w0 after changing minimum to maximum by wJ. Then
m_{k(y),k(w)}=p_{y^-1w0,w^-1w0}=p_{w0y,w0w}=p_{yw0,ww0}.
The first equality is spherical reduction, the second simultaneous inversion,
and the third longest-conjugation invariance: the Hecke automorphism
H_s→H_{w0 s w0} preserves bar and triangularity, so ordinary KL uniqueness proves
this symmetry. Thus singular blocks are spherical, not an antispherical mirror. Conjugation by w0 preserves the Hecke presentation, bar and Bruhat order; prove its KL-coefficient symmetry locally by uniqueness, then use inverse symmetry to justify the spherical dictionary k(w)=w_Jw^-1w0. Reconcile actual regular dominant-base suppliers before closure.

items.title: Parabolic category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a dominant regular
integral weight $\lambda$ of the complex type-$A$ Lie algebra and the standard
parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$, with reductive Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and longest
Levi Weyl element $w_J$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]). The
$\mathfrak p_J$-dominant weights in this regular block are exactly
$y\cdot\lambda$ for $y\in{}^JW$. Write
$\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=M_{\mathfrak p}(y\cdot\lambda)$,
$L(x\cdot\lambda)$ and $P^J(x\cdot\lambda)$ for its generalized standards,
simples and projective covers
([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]). Then for
$x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=(P^J(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1).$$

These are the antispherical sign coefficients, with support $y\le x$ and
diagonal $1$. The precise character/Grothendieck identity supplying the
formula is
$$\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}\operatorname{ch}\Delta(uy\cdot\lambda).$$

For the same highest weights in the antidominant base
$\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, the actual longest-left label is
$z=yw_0$, since $y\cdot\lambda=z\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$.
Its shortest-left encoding is $a=\mathrm{lf}(y):=w_Jyw_0\in{}^JW$, so the
weight in that encoding is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$, not
$a\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. With $b=\mathrm{lf}(x)$, the reindexed matrix is
$$\widetilde N_{a,b}:=n_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}(1)=n_{w_Jaw_0,\,w_Jbw_0}(1).$$
It is the same multiplicity matrix with both indices permuted and has reversed
support in the transported order. It is not in general $n_{a,b}(1)$.
Every label retains its explicit dot-baseweight.
The highest-weight category theorem applies also to singular integral
parabolic blocks, but this ordinary regular KL matrix formula assumes the
ambient central character is regular. No singular/parabolic category
equivalence, grading or Koszul duality is asserted.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig character formula
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the dominant regular
integral conventions of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]]. Put
$N=(n_{y,x}(1))_{y,x\in{}^JW}$, with rows indexed by generalized standards and
columns by simples in a Bruhat-compatible order
([[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]). Then $N$ is upper
unitriangular and, for each $x$,
$$\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{y\ge x}(N^{-1})_{x,y}\,\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda).$$
Its inverse entries are integers computed by the finite signed chain sum of
products of $n_{a,b}(1)$; they are weighted incidence inverses, not generally
ordinary Bruhat Mobius values. In the antidominant base $\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, set
$a=\mathrm{lf}(y)=w_Jyw_0$ and encode the same weight as
$(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. The reindexed matrix is
$\widetilde N_{a,b}=N_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$
and its inverse is reindexed by the same permutation; thus the same formula
has reversed support in the transported order. This does not replace the
entries by $n_{a,b}(1)$.
This is the ungraded
character formula for the regular parabolic block, and constructs no Koszul or
Ext grading.
items.strategy: Invert the unchanged ordinary antispherical multiplicity matrix N in its dominant shortest-left labels. Under shortest-left encoding a=lf(y) of longest-left anti-base label yw0, use weight (w_Ja) dot lambda_anti and conjugate N and N^-1 by the same permutation matrix. Do not substitute n_ab for reindexed entries. Retain signed-chain inverse and no-Koszul conclusions.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials for S_3 modulo S_2
items.statement: Take $W=S_3$ with simple reflections $s_1,s_2$, let $J=\{s_1\}$, so $W_J=\{1,s_1\}$ and the minimal left coset representatives are ${^JW}=\{e,\ s_2,\ s_2s_1\}$. In the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] the two parabolic families are computed from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ (all ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of comparable pairs in $S_3$ equal $1$): the **antispherical (sign)** coefficients are $$n_{e,e}=1,\quad n_{e,s_2}=v,\quad n_{e,s_2s_1}=0,\quad n_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero; the **spherical** coefficients are $$m_{e,e}=1,\quad m_{e,s_2}=v,\quad m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2},\quad m_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero. At $v=1$ the antispherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and the spherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$. The two families therefore already differ for this smallest nontrivial parabolic: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=0$ while $m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$.
items.strategy: Finite computation inside $H_v(3)$. The ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ are known from [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] and the fact that all ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of $S_3$ equal $1$: $p_{y,x}=v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}$ for $y\le x$ and zero otherwise, so the only nonzero values needed are $p_{e,e}=1$, $p_{e,s_1}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, $p_{e,s_1s_2}=p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$, $p_{e,w_0}=v^{3}$, $p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_2,s_1s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_2,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=p_{s_2s_1,w_0}=v$, and the diagonal ones $1$. The antispherical coefficients are the alternating sums $n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{zy,x}$ of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]. For $y=e$: $n_{e,e}=p_{e,e}=1$, $n_{e,s_2}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v\cdot v=0$. For $y=s_2$: $n_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2}=1$ (the second term vanishes since $\ell(s_1s_2)>\ell(s_2)$), and $n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2s_1}=v-0=v$, the second term vanishing because $s_1s_2$ and $s_2s_1$ are distinct of equal length. For $y=s_2s_1$: $n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{w_0,s_2s_1}=1-0=1$, the second term vanishing by the support condition. The spherical coefficients are $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$ ([[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]): $m_{e,e}=p_{s_1,s_1}=1$, $m_{e,s_2}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=v$, $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $m_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_1s_2,s_1s_2}=1$, $m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=v$, $m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{w_0,w_0}=1$. All arithmetic is in $\mathbb Z[v]$ with the Bruhat comparabilities of $S_3$ ([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]]); the coset set is ${^JW}=\{e,s_2,s_2s_1\}$ ([[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]). An independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$, from the bar involution and the induced-module standard bases, reproduces both tables.

items.title: Spherical and antispherical normalizations give different polynomials
items.statement: For $W=S_3$ and $J=\{s_1\}$ the spherical and antispherical parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] are not the same, and not merely by a unit: for the pair $y=e$, $x=s_2s_1\in{^JW}$ one has $$n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0\neq m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2},$$ evaluated at $v=1$: the antispherical value vanishes while the spherical value is $1$. The value $n_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=0$ is not a unit multiple of $m_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=1$, and the two coefficients differ as polynomials, so the discrepancy is not an artifact of specializing at $v=1$. Consequently the two normalizations cannot be substituted for one another in a multiplicity statement: a singular-block or parabolic multiplicity theorem must fix the side of the parabolic and the corresponding module (trivial versus sign). In particular the singular-block multiplicity theorem of this page is stated in the spherical normalization whereas genuine regular parabolic locally-finite category O uses the antispherical family with the explicit dominant-base labels, so using the antispherical value $n_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=0$ in place of the spherical $m_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=1$ produces a false multiplicity.
items.strategy: Two-term computation in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$, using the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients $p_{r,s}=v^{\ell(s)-\ell(r)}$ for comparable pairs and zero otherwise. Antispherical: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=\sum_{z\in\{1,s_1\}}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{z,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}$ by [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]; here $p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$ and $s_1\le s_2s_1$ with length gap one, so $p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$ and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0$. Spherical: $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$ by the reduction $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$. The coset set and Bruhat relations are those of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]] and [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]; the values were checked by an independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$ via the triangular construction of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The conclusion is a counterexample to any normalization-blind statement of the parabolic multiplicity theorem, not to the theorems themselves.

items.title: Translation to a singular wall in type A_2
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and use the coordinate
$l=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, so the dot action is $s\cdot l=-l-2$
and the facets are $(-\infty,-1)$, $\{-1\}$, $(-1,\infty)$
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]], Example 3.11 of
the source). Take $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$. Then the singular block
$\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)=M(-1)=P(-1)$, and the
translation functor $T=T_{-2}^{-1}$ satisfies $TM(-2)=M(-1)$, $TM(0)=M(-1)$,
$$TL(-2)=L(-1)\quad(\text{the label }1\in W^J),\qquad TL(0)=0\quad(\text{the label }s\notin W^J),$$
and $TP(-2)=2\,P(-1)$, because the projective cover $P(-2)$ of $L(-2)$ has
the Verma flag $\Delta(-2),\Delta(0)$ and both factors are sent to
$\Delta(-1)$.

For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ take $J=\{s_1\}$ and the dot-antidominant
$\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$; then $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ and by
[[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the
composition and Verma-flag matrices of the singular block are
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
in the row/column order $(1,\,s_2,\,s_1s_2)$: explicitly $M(\mu)$ is
irreducible, $M(s_2\cdot\mu)$ has composition factors $L(\mu),L(s_2\cdot\mu)$
once each, and $M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has all three simples once; dually
$(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for all three $y$,
$(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_2\cdot\mu))=(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu))=1$,
with its $\Delta(\mu)$ multiplicity zero, and
$P(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has the single top-label standard.
The surviving
simple labels are exactly the minimal coset representatives, so translation
onto the wall kills $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\notin W^J$ (for instance
$L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ case).

Since yw0<=ww0 iff y>=w, read projective flags from columns of that lower matrix: P(mu) has all3 standards, middle projective has last2, highest projective has only itself. Preserve all simple factor/wall survivor computations.

items.title: A small parabolic category O character formula
items.statement:
For $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, $\lambda=0$, $J=\{s_1\}$, the genuine regular parabolic
category has minimal-left labels $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$, with highest weights
$0,-\alpha_2,-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2$. Its generalized-standard/simple matrix is
$$N=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad N^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&1\\0&1&-1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Thus
$$\operatorname{ch}L(0)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(0)-\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_2)+\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2),$$
$\operatorname{ch}L(-\alpha_2)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_2)-\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)$,
and $\operatorname{ch}L(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)$.

For comparison retain the singular antidominant block with
$\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$ and right-minimal labels $(e,s_2,s_1s_2)$: its
composition matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has
inverse
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, giving
$\operatorname{ch}L(\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)$,
$\operatorname{ch}L(s_2\cdot\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(s_2\cdot\mu)-\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)$,
and
$\operatorname{ch}L(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)-\operatorname{ch}M(s_2\cdot\mu)$.
The latter coefficients are Mobius values in this all-one singular chain only.
The two blocks exemplify distinct spherical and antispherical formulas; the
singular example is not the generalized-Verma character formula of the
parabolic category.
items.strategy: The preceding finite Hecke example gives the antispherical N. The generalized standard highest weights follow from the dot action of s2 and s2s1 on0 and are J-dominant. Apply the repaired regular-parabolic multiplicity theorem and invert its upper matrix explicitly; both matrix products with the displayed inverse are identities. The actual finite Levi identity reads ch Delta^J(y dot0)=ch Delta(y dot0)-ch Delta(s1 y dot0) since W_J={e,s1}. Expanding ordinary S3 KL values therefore supplies N independently. Apply the repaired row-x parabolic character formula. Separately preserve the true singular composition matrix of the wall example and its explicit lower inverse; the corrected spherical k dictionary gives that matrix, and ordinary inversion supplies those singular character identities. Its all-one chain specialization is Mobius; it is not a claim that all inverse-KL matrices are ordinary Mobius. No singular/parabolic equivalence or grading is used. The singular lower matrix has entry one exactly for y>=w, not y<=w; preserve both displayed matrices and character identities.
